skill.name: agent-memory-mcp
skill.description: Provides an MCP memory service for storing, searching, retrieving, and reviewing project knowledge across AI agent sessions.
skill.summary: Store and retrieve project decisions, patterns, and architecture through an MCP memory service.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Most detections are false positives caused by Markdown backticks and MCP examples. The skill still directs users to clone, install, and run third-party code, while unrestricted persistent writes create memory-poisoning exposure.

remediation.issue: Setup executes an unpinned community repository and its npm scripts.
remediation.suggestion: Pin a reviewed commit, require a lockfile with npm ci, disclose lifecycle scripts, and request confirmation before compilation or startup.

remediation.issue: Persistent memory accepts arbitrary content without documented provenance or trust controls.
remediation.suggestion: Label memory sources, separate untrusted content, validate writes, and require confirmation before stored text influences agent instructions.

remediation.issue: Dashboard authentication and binding behavior are not documented.
remediation.suggestion: Bind explicitly to loopback, document access controls, and warn users before any network exposure.

content.user_title: Build Persistent Memory for AI Agents
content.value_statement: AI agents can lose project decisions and patterns between sessions. This skill provides searchable MCP memory for storing and retrieving durable project knowledge.
actual_capabilities: Search memories by text query, type, or tags.
Store decisions, patterns, and other project knowledge under stable keys.
Retrieve a specific stored memory by key.
Run a local dashboard for viewing memory activity.
limitations: Requires Node.js 18 or newer and the external agentMemory repository.
Requires installing dependencies and running third-party npm scripts.
Dashboard authentication and access controls are not described.
Retention, privacy, backup, and conflict-handling policies are not documented.

use_cases.title: Recover Project Decisions
use_cases.description: Search prior architecture decisions before changing an established subsystem.

use_cases.title: Preserve Engineering Patterns
use_cases.description: Record approved implementation patterns so teams can reference consistent guidance later.

use_cases.title: Review Memory Usage
use_cases.description: Inspect memory statistics and dashboard activity across an agent-assisted project.

prompt_templates.title: Search Project Memory
prompt_templates.prompt: Search memory for [topic]. Return matching keys, types, tags, and concise summaries.
prompt_templates.scenario: Begin with a focused lookup before starting related work.

prompt_templates.title: Store a Project Decision
prompt_templates.prompt: Store this decision under key [key] with type decision and tags [tags]: [decision and rationale].
prompt_templates.scenario: Preserve an approved choice for future sessions.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Stored Patterns
prompt_templates.prompt: Search for patterns tagged [tag]. Compare their purposes, constraints, and related decisions without inventing missing details.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Memory Coverage
prompt_templates.prompt: Show memory statistics, then search decisions and patterns for [project area]. Identify coverage gaps, duplicates, and entries needing human review.
prompt_templates.scenario: Review the quality and completeness of long-term project memory.

output_examples.output: Found two authentication pattern memories. One covers session validation, and one covers service-token rotation.
Stored the caching decision under the requested key with its decision type and supplied tags.
The memory bank contains decisions, patterns, and architecture entries. Counts are grouped by memory type for review.

best_practices: Use stable, descriptive keys that remain meaningful across sessions.
Add types and tags consistently so later searches return focused results.
Review stored content and provenance before using it to guide sensitive actions.
anti_patterns: Do not store secrets, credentials, or personal data in project memory.
Do not treat retrieved memories as trusted instructions without verification.
Do not install or run updated third-party code without reviewing its source and lockfile.

faq.question: What information can this skill store?
faq.answer: It can store string content under a key, type, and optional tags, including decisions, patterns, and architecture notes.

faq.question: How can I find a stored memory?
faq.answer: Search by query, optional type, or tags, or retrieve a known entry directly by key.

faq.question: Does the memory persist across sessions?
faq.answer: The skill describes persistent long-term memory, but retention and backup behavior are not documented.

faq.question: What software is required?
faq.answer: Node.js 18 or newer and the external agentMemory repository are required.

faq.question: Does it include a dashboard?
faq.answer: Yes. The documentation provides a local dashboard command and a localhost address on port 3333.

faq.question: Is stored content automatically trustworthy?
faq.answer: No. Review source, accuracy, and safety before retrieved content influences agent behavior or project changes.
